subsystem: Server data plane (server/core.sh + install.sh bootstrap; residential-helper.sh cited only for the relay's role as configured/started by core.sh)
summary: core.sh (1995 lines) writes, once at install time, two Hysteria2 instances and one Xray process with two REALITY inbounds, fronted by Caddy for the admin-panel TLS, plus a permanent local sing-box relay process that residential-labeled traffic always transits. install.sh's run_core_install() calls: install_hysteria → install_nodejs → install_nginx(=install_caddy) → install_xray → collect_user_input → configure_hysteria → configure_xray → configure_nginx_proxy(=configure_caddy_proxy) → deploy_admin_panel → create_services → start_all_services → create_global_command → install_tui_tools → harden_ssh → configure_performance → configure_system_hygiene. Two functions defined in core.sh for opening firewall ports (configure_firewall) and for static DNS (setup_static_dns) are never called anywhere in the live install path — they are pure dead weight, superseded (for DNS) by a duplicated inline block in update.sh and (for firewall) by nothing at all in the current flow, meaning ufw base-port rules for the main service ports are not actually applied by a fresh v3.5+ install unless update.sh's own migration blocks fill the gap on the next cron run. Two more functions (install_nginx, configure_nginx_proxy) are not "legacy compat" in the dead sense — they are the sole call sites used by install.sh, i.e. load-bearing but misleadingly named indirection over install_caddy/configure_caddy_proxy. The two-Hysteria / two-Xray-inbound topology, which looks at first glance like the kind of duplication the owner suspects, is actually structurally necessary given how b-ui exposes "four nodes" as four independently-dialable host:port endpoints to clients (v2rayN/sing-box pick a node = pick a TCP/UDP endpoint), not as server-side per-connection routing — Hysteria2 has one listener per config with no inbound-tag concept, and both Xray REALITY inbounds share the same UUID/email across the direct/residential split, so Xray's `user`-based routing rule cannot be used to collapse them onto one port either. The one place where a real, provable extra hop exists for zero benefit is the residential path when the residential URL pool is empty: hysteria-residential and vless-residential are *always* wired to relay through 127.0.0.1:2080 (a full sing-box process: sniff → route → re-dial), even when that relay's only configured behavior is "route everything to direct" — a job the direct-labeled instances already do in-process via their own freedom/direct outbound, no relay needed.

components.name: configure_firewall()
components.role: opens ufw/firewalld rules for SSH, hy2 base+hop ports, both xray ports, residential base port
components.evidence: Repo-wide grep `grep -rn "configure_firewall" .` (excluding its own def and the unrelated legacy b-ui-server.sh:611 definition/b-ui-server.sh:1256 self-call) returns zero call sites in install.sh, core.sh, or update.sh. install.sh's run_core_install() (install.sh:550-583) never references it.
components.simplification: Delete the function, or fold its rule set into configure_port_hopping()/start_all_services() which is the only firewall-touching code actually on the fresh-install path today.

components.name: setup_static_dns()
components.role: disables systemd-resolved, writes static /etc/resolv.conf (1.1.1.1/8.8.8.8/9.9.9.9), chattr +i locks it
components.evidence: `grep -rn \"setup_static_dns\" .` returns only its own definition — no caller in install.sh/core.sh/update.sh. The equivalent behavior is instead re-implemented inline as migration block 'D' in server/update.sh:1738-1751 (systemctl disable systemd-resolved; chattr -i; rewrite resolv.conf; chattr +i), which is the code that actually runs (via the update.sh cron path / apply_systemd_configs). A fresh v3.5+ install therefore gets no static DNS until the next 6h cron `update.sh auto` executes migration block D.
components.simplification: Delete setup_static_dns() from core.sh and have run_core_install() call update.sh's D-block logic directly (or extract it into one shared function both scripts source) so fresh installs get static DNS immediately instead of waiting up to 6h for cron.

components.name: install_chinese_fonts()
components.role: apt/yum/dnf-installs fonts-noto-cjk / google-noto-sans-cjk-sc-fonts, runs fc-cache
components.evidence: `grep -rn \"install_chinese_fonts\" .` (repo-wide) returns only the definition at core.sh:394 — zero callers in install.sh, core.sh's own run body, update.sh, or b-ui-cli.sh.
components.simplification: Delete outright; a headless proxy server has no rendering surface that needs CJK font glyphs (menu output uses ANSI/box-drawing chars via print_info/etc., not glyph rendering).

components.name: install_nginx() / configure_nginx_proxy()
components.role: one-line delegates to install_caddy() / configure_caddy_proxy()
components.evidence: install.sh:562 calls install_nginx (never install_caddy directly); install.sh:571 calls configure_nginx_proxy (never configure_caddy_proxy directly) — grep confirms these are the ONLY call sites of either name pair anywhere in server/core.sh or install.sh. So the "compat" wrapper is in fact the live, load-bearing entry point, while the real implementation names (install_caddy/configure_caddy_proxy) are only reached indirectly. Marked '兼容旧调用' (compat with old calls) in the source but nothing in the current repo calls install_caddy/configure_caddy_proxy by their real names.
components.simplification: Since v4 allows a clean reinstall, just rename install.sh's call sites to install_caddy/configure_caddy_proxy and delete the two indirection wrappers — removes a naming layer that actively misleads readers into thinking nginx is installed.

components.name: hysteria-server + hysteria-residential (two full Hysteria2 systemd instances)
components.role: two independently-listening Hysteria2 processes so client-selected 'direct' vs 'residential' nodes are two distinct dial targets, not a server-side routing decision
components.evidence: config-residential.yaml (core.sh:595-654) already proves Hysteria2 supports multi-outbound+ACL within one process (`outbounds: [relay, direct]` + `acl: inline: [relay(all)]`), so the 2-instance split is not there because ACL routing is impossible — it exists because Hysteria2's config has exactly one `listen:` line per process (no per-inbound tags like Xray), so there is no way for one process to expose two separately-dialable endpoints (:10000 vs :40000) with different fixed outbound behavior. Corroborated by two independent, asymmetric systemd resource profiles (MemoryMax=700M/GOMEMLIMIT=400MiB for direct vs 500M/200MiB for residential) and separate per-instance port-jump cleanup invocations (hy2-portjump-cleanup.sh called once per instance with a distinct base port, core.sh:216 and core.sh:277) — deliberate per-instance isolation, not accidental duplication.
components.simplification: keep

components.name: vless-direct + vless-residential (two Xray REALITY inbounds, one process)
components.role: two fixed dial ports (:10001/:10002) exposing the same account's UUID with different fixed egress
components.evidence: web/server.js:336-339 maps the SAME realityClients array (same uuid+email) onto both inbound tags vless-direct and vless-residential — routing is chosen purely by which port the client dials, not by per-connection user identity, so Xray's routing.user matcher (which needs distinct emails per route) cannot be used to collapse this to one port without giving every account two UUIDs. Two separate `port` fields inside one Xray process's `inbounds` array is the minimum structure that can expose 'same account, two egress choices' as two independently selectable v2rayN/sing-box server entries.
components.simplification: keep — a real simplification would require reworking how subscriptions present nodes to clients (e.g. per-node UUIDs + Xray `user` routing) which is a client-protocol change, not a server dead-weight cut

components.name: b-ui-relay sing-box process routing residential traffic when the URL pool is empty
components.location: server/residential-helper.sh:462-504 (write_singbox_config_direct), core.sh's hysteria-residential outbound relay(core.sh:641-645) and xray vless-residential outbound relay(core.sh:830)
components.role: unconditional extra local hop (sniff+route+re-dial through 127.0.0.1:2080) for 100% of residential-labeled connections, even in fail-open empty-pool mode where the relay's only rule is 'everything → direct'
components.evidence: hysteria-residential's outbound is hardcoded to `socks5 127.0.0.1:2080` (core.sh:642-645, `acl: relay(all)` — unconditional, not conditioned on pool state) and vless-residential's outbound is hardcoded to the xray `relay` tag → `socks 127.0.0.1:2080` (core.sh:830, `routing.rules` unconditionally sends inboundTag vless-residential to outboundTag relay, core.sh:836). When the pool is empty, residential-helper.sh writes write_singbox_config_direct() (residential-helper.sh:462-504), whose entire route table reduces to `"final": "direct"` — i.e. the relay process does nothing but add a socket hop + DNS-over-UDP resolve + sniff step that hysteria-server/vless-direct already skip by dialing `freedom`/`direct mode:4` in-process (core.sh:584-588, core.sh:829).
components.simplification: When the residential pool is empty, point hysteria-residential's and vless-residential's outbound at their own in-process direct egress (mirroring the -direct instances) instead of through the relay, and only rewire them to the relay socks/http outbound once a real upstream is enabled — cuts one process hop + one extra local dial off every residential-labeled connection for accounts that haven't turned residential on (the v4-fresh-install default state).

claims_to_verify: configure_firewall() at server/core.sh:1237-1283 is defined but has zero callers anywhere in install.sh, server/core.sh, or server/update.sh (repo-wide grep for the literal string 'configure_firewall' outside its own definition and the unrelated legacy b-ui-server.sh finds nothing).

setup_static_dns() at server/core.sh:1289-1319 is defined but never called from install.sh/core.sh/update.sh; the same static-DNS behavior (disable systemd-resolved, rewrite /etc/resolv.conf, chattr +i) is separately re-implemented as migration block D inside server/update.sh:1738-1751, which is the code path that actually executes.
install_chinese_fonts() at server/core.sh:394-410 is defined but has no callers anywhere in the repo (repo-wide grep for 'install_chinese_fonts' returns only its own definition line).

install.sh:562 and install.sh:571 call install_nginx()/configure_nginx_proxy() (server/core.sh:364/914), which are one-line delegates to install_caddy()/configure_caddy_proxy() (server/core.sh:328/849); install_caddy and configure_caddy_proxy are never called by their real names anywhere in install.sh or core.sh.

web/server.js:334-339 assigns the same uuid/email pair to both the vless-direct and vless-residential Xray inbound tags when building xray-config.json, meaning the direct/residential choice for a given account is encoded purely by which of ports :10001/:10002 the client dials, not by any server-side per-connection routing rule.

hysteria-residential's outbound in server/core.sh:641-653 is an unconditional `acl: inline: [relay(all)]` pointing at socks5 127.0.0.1:2080, and Xray's vless-residential inbound is unconditionally routed to outboundTag 'relay' -> socks 127.0.0.1:2080 in server/core.sh:830-836, so residential-labeled traffic always transits the b-ui-relay sing-box process even when residential-helper.sh's write_singbox_config_direct() (server/residential-helper.sh:462-504) configures that relay to do nothing but forward everything to 'direct'.
topology_notes:
Listener/port table (all IPv4-only egress per CLAUDE.md; no IPv6 anywhere in this subsystem):
- hysteria-server (config.yaml): UDP :${PORT:-10000} (+ UDP ${PORT_HOPPING_START:-20000}-${PORT_HOPPING_END:-30000} in the same `listen:` line, core.sh:527-530) — TLS via shared Caddy-issued cert; auth http→ (installer-time) rewritten to local userpass by apply_hy2_userpass_auth (core.sh:669-692); trafficStats 127.0.0.1:9999; outbound `direct` mode 4 (IPv4-only, core.sh:584-588).
- hysteria-residential (config-residential.yaml): UDP :40000 (+ UDP 41000-50000, core.sh:531,600) — same TLS/auth pattern; trafficStats 127.0.0.1:9998; outbound unconditionally `relay`→socks5 127.0.0.1:2080 via `acl: relay(all)` (core.sh:641-653).
- xray (single process, xray-config.json, core.sh:775-841): dokodemo-door API inbound 127.0.0.1:10085 (tag `api`, feeds Xray's own StatsService/HandlerService); `vless-direct` TCP :10001 REALITY (dest=masq_domain:443) → outbound `direct` (freedom, domainStrategy ForceIPv4); `vless-residential` TCP :10002 REALITY (same dest/keys/shortId) → outbound `relay` (socks 127.0.0.1:2080).
- Caddy: TCP 80/443 on ${DOMAIN} → reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:${ADMIN_PORT:-8080} (admin panel only); also drives Caddy's own ACME issuance whose certs are synced out-of-band to /opt/b-ui/certs for hysteria's TLS (setup_cert_sync, core.sh:923-1040) — Caddy itself never terminates hysteria/xray traffic and the REALITY masquerade domain (default www.bing.com) is an unrelated third-party site Xray/Hysteria mimic in the TLS ClientHello, not proxied through Caddy.
- b-ui-admin (Node, b-ui-admin.service): binds 127.0.0.1:${ADMIN_PORT}, reached only via Caddy reverse_proxy — not directly firewall-exposed.
- b-ui-relay (sing-box, started/rewritten by residential-helper.sh, not core.sh): SOCKS inbound 127.0.0.1:2080 (both residential Hysteria and residential Xray dial into this); Clash API 127.0.0.1:9091 (used by resi-health.sh, never opened externally). Egress is either its own `direct` outbound (pool empty) or a `resi-pool` selector of external socks5/http upstream URLs (pool non-empty).
- cert-sync/hy2-watchdog/cert-check: three independent triggers converge on the same cert-sync.sh / hysteria-restart action — b-ui-cert-sync.timer (systemd, OnBootSec=30s then every 6h, core.sh:1020-1033), cron `cert-check.sh` (every 12h, calls the same /opt/b-ui/cert-sync.sh, core.sh:1193-1195), and the one-off `wait_and_sync_certs` call during install (core.sh:1813) — three overlapping, idempotent paths to the same effect (cert sync + restart hy2 if changed); harmless (cmp-gated, restarts only on real change) but is exactly the kind of accreted-redundant scheduling the owner is describing, worth consolidating to one timer.
- Firewall: ufw/firewalld rules for the base ports (22, PORT, 80/443, 10001/10002, 40000) are only ever opened by the dead configure_firewall() — meaning on a v3.5+ install with ufw pre-enabled, only the two hop ranges get opened (once, redundantly, by both configure_firewall-equivalent-never-run and by configure_port_hopping which only covers the direct-instance hop range, core.sh:1406-1417 — note it does NOT open the residential hop range 41000-50000 either).
- sysctl/conntrack/BBR tuning (configure_performance, core.sh:1443-1527) is single-sourced, no duplication found; conntrack table size scales with detected RAM (131072/262144/524288) and explicitly reserves the proxy port ranges from the ephemeral port pool to avoid self-collision — a genuinely load-bearing, non-redundant piece for multi-hundred-user scale.
scaling_concerns: net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max caps at 524288 for boxes with >4096MB RAM (core.sh:1506) — with hy2 port-hopping meaning each client's UDP QUIC session can span multiple 5-tuples plus DNAT-adjacent conntrack entries, a genuinely 'thousands of concurrent users' target should verify this ceiling empirically rather than trust the tier breakpoints, which look tuned for the current handful of users per CLAUDE.md's mainland-China two-server description.

b-ui-admin (Node, single process) is explicitly capped at MemoryHigh=150M/MemoryMax=200M (core.sh:1754-1755) while also being the single point that authenticates every hysteria connection at install time before the switch to local userpass auth — the comment at core.sh:660 already documents this SPOF risk under reconnect storms; if a future release regresses back to http auth callbacks (or a per-request path still hits the panel, e.g. traffic accounting polling under 1000+ users), the 200M ceiling could become the actual scale limit rather than proxy throughput.

The relay-hop redundancy on residential nodes (see REDUNDANT finding above) means every residential-labeled connection for every user pays one extra local process hop unconditionally; at scale (1000s of users, many likely on the residential node for the AI-domain use case) this is 1000s of extra long-lived local socket pairs + sniff/route CPU cycles inside b-ui-relay that buys nothing when the pool is off — a real, multiplying inefficiency at the user counts the owner is targeting, not just a one-time install-time nit.

Two live Hysteria2 processes plus one Xray process plus one sing-box relay plus Node admin panel plus Caddy = 5 long-running services status-checked/restarted by three overlapping timers (cert-sync timer, cert-check cron, hy2-watchdog timer) — at 1000s of users, restart-on-cert-change (core.sh:989-996) restarts BOTH hy2 instances on every cert renewal regardless of which one's traffic is affected (they share one cert), which is unavoidable given the shared-cert design but is a synchronized full-outage blip for all direct+residential hy2 users simultaneously every renewal — worth confirming Caddy's renewal cadence doesn't collide with peak hours at scale.
metrics: core.sh: 1995 lines total, ~46 top-level functions. install.sh: 869 lines. update.sh: 2327 lines (not this subsystem's focus). residential-helper.sh: 858 lines, ~25 functions (cited only for the relay it configures). Confirmed-dead functions in core.sh: configure_firewall (47 lines, 1237-1283), setup_static_dns (31 lines, 1289-1319), install_chinese_fonts (17 lines, 394-410) — 95 combined dead lines out of 1995 (~4.8%). Redundant-indirection functions: install_nginx/configure_nginx_proxy (2+4 lines of pure delegation, but load-bearing as the only call path — not deletable without an install.sh edit). Data-plane listeners: 2 Hysteria2 UDP listeners (+2 hop ranges), 2 Xray TCP REALITY inbounds (1 process), 1 Caddy TCP 80/443, 1 sing-box relay SOCKS+ClashAPI (2 loopback ports) = 6 external-facing ports (22 excluded) + 5 loopback-only ports (8080 admin, 9999/9998 hy2 stats, 10085 xray api, 2080/9091 relay). Cert-sync/health redundancy: 3 independent trigger mechanisms (systemd timer every 6h, cron every 12h, one-shot at install) all converging on the same idempotent cert-sync.sh script.

subsystem: B-UI server control plane: server/update.sh, server/b-ui-cli.sh, install.sh
summary: This subsystem is the server-side upgrade/bootstrap control plane: install.sh (first-run bootstrap + dispatcher), server/core.sh (fresh-install generator, sourced by install.sh), server/update.sh (the auto-updater sourced by cron and by b-ui-cli.sh, holding apply_systemd_configs()'s ~25 named migration blocks), and server/b-ui-cli.sh (the `sudo b-ui` admin CLI, which sources update.sh at runtime for its own update/kernel-update menu items). On the wire it only ever talks to GitHub (raw.githubusercontent.com / raw.githack.com / api.github.com) and a few release-asset hosts (get.hy2.sh, Xray-install, gum/fzf GitHub releases) to pull files and version metadata; all its real work is local: writing systemd units/drop-ins, sysctl.d files, crontab entries, sshd_config.d, fail2ban/journald config, and the Hysteria2/Xray/sing-box config files that the data plane actually serves traffic through. Architecturally the defect the owner is pointing at is real and provable: core.sh (fresh install) and update.sh (upgrade self-heal) are two independently-maintained code paths that were never unified, so almost everything core.sh writes at install time has a byte-for-byte or near-byte-for-byte twin re-implemented as a version-gated 'migration block' in update.sh's apply_systemd_configs(), which then runs unconditionally on every 6-hour cron tick on every server forever — even once every guard condition it checks for has become permanently unsatisfiable on the current fleet. Roughly 30% of update.sh's 2327 lines fall into this bucket today. A second, smaller pattern is straightforward logic triplication (SSH hardening exists independently in core.sh, update.sh, and b-ui-cli.sh; cron-entry writing exists independently in core.sh, update.sh, and install.sh) where every copy is technically reachable but none should exist as a separate copy. A third pattern is one genuinely misplaced but non-dead block (D8, residential health-timer reconciliation) that is not a version migration at all but live state reconciliation wrongly filed alongside the legacy blocks. The install_type==0 'ancient single-file install' migration path in install.sh is fully dead given the current fleet's history. Net effect: the owner's instinct ('堆山') is well-founded — the file has accreted a parallel implementation of core.sh for every version bump instead of ever refactoring to share code, and the fix is mechanical (extract shared functions, delete version guards below the fleet's current floor) rather than a redesign.

components.name: apply_systemd_configs()
components.role: Master reconciliation function called on every update.sh invocation (do_update, auto_update, check_and_update's no-op branch) — 1034 lines, ~44% of the file, containing ~25 named migration blocks (D1-D9, A/A.fix/A.fix2, B/B.fix, C, D, E, migrate_admin_env, migrate_ssh_hardening, migrate_relay_log, migrate_ipv4_only_egress, cert-sync rewrite, hy2-watchdog deploy, patch_resi_health_timer).
components.evidence: CLAUDE.md: 'apply_systemd_configs() runs on every update (including already latest)'. git log top commit is 'v3.6.2'; task brief states both prod servers run v3.6.3. Every migration block inside targets a version <= v3.6.0 (see child components below), each already satisfied by core.sh's fresh-install output (grep confirmed for every block, see claims_to_verify). So on every 6h cron tick, ~700 of these 1034 lines (~30% of the whole file) run pure no-op grep/stat/jq checks against conditions that provably cannot occur on the current fleet.
components.simplification: Collapse into a small set of permanent 'ensure_<thing>' idempotent functions shared (via a sourced lib) with core.sh's install-time generators, so fresh-install and upgrade-apply are literally the same function calls. Delete every block whose guard targets a version < v3.6.2 given the owner's accepted v4 clean-reinstall decision (D1,D3,D4,D5,D6,D7,D9,migrate_admin_env,migrate_ssh_hardening,migrate_relay_log,A,A.fix2,B,B.fix,C,D,E,hy2-watchdog-deploy-guard,cert-sync-rewrite-guard,update_service_paths). Keep only the genuinely version-independent reconciliation logic: D8 (residential health timer membership check), the config-integrity repair in repair_hysteria_config, and the 'warn on stale custom keywords' half of migrate_residential_keywords.

components.name: D6: hy2 http→userpass auth migration (inline awk)
components.role: Rewrites config.yaml/config-residential.yaml auth block from http-callback to local userpass for pre-v3.5.15 installs.
components.evidence: The awk script at update.sh:1108 (`/^auth:/ {print "auth:"; print "  type: userpass"...`) is character-for-character identical to core.sh's apply_hy2_userpass_auth() awk script at core.sh:684, which core.sh now calls at install time (core.sh:662, comment: '原本等首次面板存用户才切，这里提前到安装期' = 'originally waited for first panel save, now moved up to install time'). Both guard on the same `grep -qE '^  type: http$'` pattern.
components.simplification: Delete the D6 block entirely; have update.sh source core.sh (or a shared lib) and call apply_hy2_userpass_auth() directly. This is the single cleanest, lowest-risk dedup: one function, two callers, zero behavior change.

components.name: SSH hardening (triple implementation)
components.role: Writes /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/00-b-ui-hardening.conf (disable password auth) when a pubkey is present; three call sites: install-time, every update.sh apply cycle, and manual `sudo b-ui harden-ssh`.
components.evidence: All three functions contain the same ~40-line body (pubkey-count grep, 00-prefix rationale comment word-for-word identical, identical heredoc content, identical sshd -t rollback logic) with only cosmetic differences (print_error vs print_warning, exit vs return). None is dead (all three are independently reachable: install, cron self-heal, manual subcommand) so this is pure logic triplication, not dead code.
components.simplification: Extract to one `ensure_ssh_hardening()` in a shared lib sourced by all three files.

components.name: install_tui_tools() duplicate
components.role: Downloads gum+fzf TUI binaries from GitHub releases.
components.evidence: update.sh's copy is only invoked from the bottom `case "${1:-}" in ... *) ... install_tui_tools ...` block guarded by `[[ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" == "${0}" ]]` (update.sh:2299-2326), i.e. only when update.sh is executed directly with no args. Every real call site sources update.sh instead: b-ui-cli.sh:511/520 (`source "${BASE_DIR}/update.sh"`), install.sh:793. Cron always passes `auto`/`kernel` args. So in the sourced-usage pattern that covers every automated and CLI-menu path, this copy's function body is loaded but its only caller is unreachable. The two copies have also already drifted: install.sh's extracts the binary via `find "$tmp" -name gum` (install.sh:716) while update.sh's assumes a fixed `$tmp/gum` path (update.sh:2263) — a real behavioral difference from parallel maintenance.
components.simplification: Delete the update.sh copy; keep only install.sh's (more robust) version, invoked once at fresh install. If self-heal for missing gum/fzf on old installs is wanted, call it from apply_systemd_configs conditionally instead of duplicating the whole downloader.

components.name: update_service_paths() + install_type==0 legacy-install migration
components.location: install.sh:343-463 (migrate_old_path, check_old_version, update_service_paths) and install.sh:784-790 (case branch); server/update.sh:368-406 (duplicate update_service_paths)
components.role: Detects and migrates a pre-modular single-file b-ui install at /opt/hysteria (no version.json) to /opt/b-ui.
components.evidence: check_old_version() (install.sh:424-463) classifies a host as install_type=0 only if `/usr/local/bin/b-ui` exists AND `${BASE_DIR}/version.json` is absent. CLAUDE.md states the actual legacy artifact, `b-ui-server.sh` (all-in-one, installs to /opt/hysteria), 'is not in version.json's file list, not used by install.sh' — i.e. it is a disconnected product that never created a `/opt/b-ui` version.json-bearing install in the first place, so no real upgrade path lands in install_type==0 today. Both production servers (per user memory: bwg-rick reinstalled 2026-06-03, bwg-tizi long-running v3.x) carry version.json and would hit install_type==1. `update_service_paths` itself (both copies) greps live unit files for the literal string `/opt/hysteria`, a string that cannot reappear once removed.
components.simplification: Delete migrate_old_path, check_old_version's install_type==0 branch, and both copies of update_service_paths, given the owner's accepted v4 clean-reinstall decision.

components.name: D9 migrate_ipv4_only_egress()
components.role: Adds IPv4-only direct egress (hy2 `direct.mode:4`, xray `domainStrategy:ForceIPv4`) to configs generated before v3.6.0.
components.evidence: core.sh already emits this on every fresh/re-install: config.yaml direct block at core.sh:588 (`mode: 4`), config-residential.yaml at core.sh:649, xray direct outbound at core.sh:829 (`"domainStrategy": "ForceIPv4"`). Comment at update.sh:417 confirms: 'D9 迁移即为幂等空操作' (D9 migration is already an idempotent no-op) for anything core.sh-generated. Both prod servers are already >= v3.6.2, i.e. past this threshold.

topology_notes:
Control-plane call graph (not the data-plane traffic topology):
- Cron (root crontab, written by core.sh:configure_cron_tasks / update.sh:ensure_cron_jobs / install.sh inline fallback) fires `update.sh auto` every 6h and `update.sh kernel` every 12h, both as direct execution (BASH_SOURCE[0]==$0) hitting the bottom case dispatcher (update.sh:2299-2326).
- `sudo b-ui` (server/b-ui-cli.sh, symlinked from /usr/local/bin/b-ui) is a separate always-resident admin entrypoint that `source`s update.sh at runtime (b-ui-cli.sh:511,520) to reuse its functions — this sourcing, not exec, is why b-ui-cli.sh's own like-named `update_kernel()` gets transparently overwritten by update.sh's version at call time.
- install.sh is the only entrypoint that `source`s core.sh (install.sh:557, and again defensively at install.sh:841 before cron setup) — update.sh and b-ui-cli.sh never source core.sh, which is exactly why they carry independent re-implementations of anything core.sh also does (sysctl files, systemd units, SSH hardening, cron writing) instead of calling core.sh's functions directly.
- Both GITHUB_RAW/GITHUB_CDN download-source selection and file-list arrays are independently declared in all three of install.sh, update.sh's do_update(), and update.sh's auto_update() (three separate `files`/`file_map` bash arrays enumerating the same ~14 remote paths) — a fourth duplicate of the same file inventory that version.json is nominally supposed to be the single source of truth for, per CLAUDE.md's own 'Important Conventions' section.
- No component in this subsystem talks to the data-plane services (hysteria-server, hysteria-residential, xray, b-ui-relay) except via `systemctl restart/start/is-active`; all config mutation is direct file writes (cat heredoc / sed / awk / jq) with a `cp` backup convention (`*.bak.<ver>.<ts>`), no shared locking against b-ui-admin's own concurrent config writes (server.js) other than the unrelated `.relay.lock` used only by residential-helper.sh.
- No IPv6, DNS or egress-path logic lives in this subsystem beyond what's inherited from core.sh's generated configs (control plane doesn't itself open sockets); its only network egress is outbound curl to GitHub (raw.githubusercontent.com, raw.githack.com, api.github.com) and get.hy2.sh / Xray-install / gum / fzf release URLs, all unauthenticated and each individually rate-limited by GitHub's anonymous 60 req/hour ceiling per source IP.
scaling_concerns: server/update.sh:2200-2203 and server/update.sh:316-320 run `npm install` on every update cycle (6h cron + every manual update) even when nothing in web/ changed, wasting I/O/CPU on every server every cycle forever — a pure efficiency defect, not a correctness one, but directly answers the owner's '提升效率' ask.

apply_systemd_configs() (server/update.sh:756-1789) executes its full ~1034-line, ~25-block gauntlet of grep/awk/jq checks unconditionally on every 6h cron tick per server, of which roughly 700 lines are now provably permanent no-ops on the current fleet (see claims_to_verify) — this cost scales linearly with server count once decision #2 (multi-server) is acted on, since each server independently re-runs the same dead checks with no central coordination.

The crontab read-modify-write pattern (three independent implementations: server/core.sh:1162-1230, server/update.sh:2030-2071, install.sh:848-853) is not atomic against a concurrent writer (e.g. an interactive `sudo b-ui` update running while the 6h cron auto_update fires) — low probability today at single-server scale, but a real race once multiple admins or automation touch the same host.

Kernel/version probing (gh_latest_tag, server/update.sh:1808-1811) hits api.github.com unauthenticated; GitHub's 60 req/hour anonymous limit is per source IP, so this is fine for one server today but becomes a shared bottleneck the moment decision #2 (multi-server) puts several production hosts behind the same egress IP or a shared monitoring/build host that also polls GitHub.

Migration fixes only reach existing installs on the next 6h cron tick (documented tradeoff, CLAUDE.md), meaning any server-side security or correctness fix has up to a 6h exposure window across the whole fleet with no push mechanism — acceptable at today's 2-server scale, a real operational gap for a 'mature product serving thousands of users' where faster-than-cron remediation (e.g. an urgent CVE fix) may be needed.

summary: b-ui-client.sh (5810 lines) is one bash file covering: self-download/bootstrap, core binary install (hysteria/xray/sing-box via 5-tier smart_download fallback), URI parsing (hysteria2://, vless://), two mutually-exclusive proxy transports (SOCKS via hysteria-client.service/xray-client.service vs full-tunnel TUN via bui-tun.service running sing-box), a numeric TUI (tui_*) wired through tui_main_loop, CLI subcommands (switch/tun/import/start/stop/status/list) for scripting/cron, a health-check systemd timer, a 3-source-parallel self-updater, and uninstall. On the wire, exactly one of {hysteria-client.service, xray-client.service, bui-tun.service} runs at a time (systemd Conflicts=), each listening on 127.0.0.1:SOCKS_PORT/HTTP_PORT (SOCKS mode) or as a TUN interface owning the default route + DNS (TUN mode, schema-versioned config at TUN_SCHEMA_VERSION=8). The single biggest finding is a ~1,331-line (23% of the file) fully dead subtree: a pre-TUI "old menu" implementation (import_node/service_control_menu/show_status/config_management/switch_config/delete_config/list_configs/import_from_subscription/import_batch/activate_imported_config/_configure_and_save/quick_install/configure_client/import_from_uri) that the numeric-TUI rewrite (tui_import_node, tui_service_control, show_status_bar, tui_switch_node, cmd_import/cmd_switch/cmd_list) was supposed to replace via thin delegation (per docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-07-cli-redesign.md, which literally specifies `tui_import_node() { import_node; }`) but instead the rewrite duplicated the logic inline and abandoned the old functions in place, unreferenced. A second, smaller dead cluster (check_dependencies + check_and_install_dep, 152 lines) means system-dependency auto-install (dig/ss/iptables/wget) never actually runs. Three more small functions (print_banner, tui_write, get_server_ip, get_current_ssh_ip) are isolated orphans. Live logic is heavily but explicably battle-hardened: the SOCKS/TUN mutual-exclusion dance (disable/enable both client units + stop/start the health timer + UFW toggle, each with its own polling/rollback) is duplicated near-verbatim across 6 call sites (cmd_stop, switch_config-equivalent _switch_to_profile, uninstall, service_control_menu-equivalent tui_service_control, auto_update_all, toggle_tun/start_tun_mode/stop_tun_mode) with no shared "stop_all_client_services" helper. TUN_SCHEMA_VERSION's own changelog (v1→v8, lines 1342-1358) documents at least 3 real flip-flops from production incidents (keyword-vs-suffix domain matching, cloudflared QUIC misdetection, and a 2026-03-20 "delete interface_name as unnecessary" regression that silently broke TUN readiness detection for 3 versions) — these are the honest cost of running for real users, not sloppiness, and should not be deleted, only consolidated.

topology_notes: Three mutually-exclusive local listeners, never concurrent (systemd Conflicts=): hysteria-client.service (SOCKS 127.0.0.1:${SOCKS_PORT:-1080} + HTTP 127.0.0.1:${HTTP_PORT:-8080}, config /opt/hysteria-client/config.yaml, upstream = the active node's Hysteria2 server:port from the imported hysteria2:// URI); xray-client.service (same SOCKS/HTTP ports, config /opt/hysteria-client/xray-config.json, upstream = the active node's VLESS-REALITY server:port); bui-tun.service (sing-box, config /opt/hysteria-client/singbox-tun.json, TUN interface literally named `bui-tun` via interface_name — a schema-8 fix after 3 versions of silent breakage from sing-box auto-naming it tun0 — owns default route + DNS, IPv6 ::/0 takeover when host_ipv6_enabled() detects a real v6 uplink, otherwise IPv4-only; egresses to whichever node protocol is active via the same URI-derived server/port). No listener accepts inbound connections from the network — all three are localhost-bound SOCKS/HTTP or a local TUN device; the only outbound network path from the client host is to the configured server:port (Hysteria2 QUIC/UDP or Xray REALITY/TCP) plus, during download/update, to GitHub/ghproxy mirrors or the user's own panel domain over HTTPS. /etc/profile.d/proxy.sh is a side-effect-only env-var file for shell sessions, not a network component. hysteria-health.timer (1-min systemd timer) and the client self-updater (check_client_update's 3-source parallel curl race, plus periodic auto_update_all via cron — ensure_client_cron) are the only components that make unsolicited outbound calls independent of user action.
scaling_concerns: N/A at 1000-user scale in the traditional sense — b-ui-client.sh runs entirely on each individual user's own Linux box, not on the shared VPS; it has no multi-tenancy, no shared state, and does not degrade as the user base grows. The 'scale' risk here is entirely maintainability/support-load: with ~23% of the file (1331 lines) being dead orphaned code that mirrors live functionality under different names (list_configs vs cmd_list/tui_switch_node's inline loop; import_node vs tui_import_node; service_control_menu vs tui_service_control), any contributor grepping for 'where does X happen' has roughly even odds of landing in the dead copy and wasting time, or worse, patching the dead copy and shipping a fix that never reaches users — this is a support/velocity risk that compounds as the user base and support-ticket volume grow, not a runtime scaling risk.

The health-check asymmetry (hysteria-health.timer only watches hysteria-client.service, never xray-client.service — b-ui-client.sh:3960-3970 vs generate_xray_config:1287-1333) means VLESS-REALITY users get zero auto-recovery from a crashed/hung client process; at 1000 users, if VLESS-REALITY is the more common node type (Xray/REALITY is generally recommended over Hysteria2 for stealth in China), that's a meaningful fraction of the user base with no self-healing SOCKS client, translating directly into avoidable support tickets ('my proxy just stopped working').

The mutual-exclusion dance's reliance on `systemctl disable`+`enable` pairs around every TUN toggle (to dodge the documented v3.6.0 boot-race where systemd Conflicts= can drop either unit) is inherently racy under concurrent invocation — e.g., cron's auto_update_all firing mid-toggle, or the user running the TUI in two SSH sessions simultaneously — and the two-transport-implementation design multiplies the number of interacting moving parts (2 client units + 1 TUN unit + 1 health timer + UFW state file) that must all agree on 'whose turn it is.' Collapsing to one sing-box-only transport (SOCKS inbound + optional TUN inbound in the same process/config) would remove this whole class of race by construction, which matters more as install count grows and the long tail of edge-case host configurations (custom UFW rules, non-systemd inits under WSL, etc.) grows with it.

scaling_concerns: A brand-new install that is handed >=2 residential upstream URLs immediately at setup time runs with NO automatic upstream failover (b-ui-resi-health.timer) for up to 6 hours, until the first cron-triggered update.sh run creates it (server/update.sh:1141-1193 is the only place that creates the timer; install.sh's fresh path never runs update.sh, see components list). For a product meant to serve 1000s of paying users, a residential upstream going bad in the first few hours after signup/setup would silently degrade (or 403-fail, given the global-mode gap below) with no self-healing until the timer exists.

In global=true mode (the ONLY mode the owner's production servers run, per user MEMORY.md), the relay routes literally everything to the residential upstream with no exception list, and docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-11-residential-auto-blacklist-design.md documents a real production observation (2026-09-11, bwg-tizi relay logs) of ~256 `403 Forbidden` rejections per 30 minutes for targets the residential provider itself refuses to proxy (Google search, Apple push :5228/:5223, payment processors) — i.e. global mode as currently shipped has a known correctness gap for a meaningful slice of real traffic; the fix (R13 auto-blacklist) is approved but NOT YET IMPLEMENTED, so this is a live gap, not a hypothetical one, and should be prioritized alongside any topology simplification since it affects every global-mode user today.

resi-health.sh's probe cadence (every ~2min via systemd timer, RESI_HEALTH_TRIES=2 attempts per member per run) issues 2 outbound HTTPS probes through EVERY residential upstream member every 2 minutes regardless of how many members exist; at a handful of upstreams this is negligible, but if the product scales to many parallel upstream pools (e.g. per-region or per-tier residential pools for 1000s of users) this is an O(members) serial-in-a-single-script probe loop (resi-health.sh:56-98 is a `while read` loop, not parallelized) that could start taking non-trivial wall-clock time per run; today's design (2-8 members typical) doesn't hit this, but it's the kind of thing that silently degrades health-check freshness as member count grows.

The relay's resi-pool selector picks the FIRST healthy member in relay-outbound-order on failover (resi-health.sh:129 `target="${healthy[0]}"`), not a least-loaded or round-robin choice; with a single relay serving all of a server's users, once a switch happens every user's traffic moves to that same one member simultaneously — fine at current single-upstream-per-tier scale, but a concentration risk if 1000s of users are meant to share a handful of residential upstreams (thundering-herd onto whichever member is 'first' and healthy).

subsystem: residential egress (server/residential-helper.sh, server/resi-health.sh, residential parts of web/server.js + web/app.js)
summary: On the wire, residential egress is two fixed, install-time-only server inbounds (hysteria-residential :40000+41000-50000, xray vless-residential :10002 REALITY) that ALWAYS forward to a local SOCKS5 relay at 127.0.0.1:2080 — core.sh writes this wiring once and residential-helper.sh never touches it again. That relay is a permanent sing-box process (b-ui-relay.service) whose OWN config (singbox-relay.json) is the only thing residential-helper.sh rewrites: it contains a `resi-pool` `selector` outbound (deliberately not sing-box's built-in `urltest`, to avoid mid-session IP switches during sensitive AI-login flows) fronting one `socks` or `http` outbound per configured residential upstream (resi-1, resi-2, ...). Routing to that pool is either unconditional (global=true: route.final=resi-pool) or keyword-gated (global=false: domain_keyword match → resi-pool, else direct) — and BOTH of the owner's production servers run global=true. A separate systemd-timer script, resi-health.sh, probes each pool member every ~2 minutes and — using only the relay's own Clash HTTP API on 127.0.0.1:9091 — flips the selector's active choice when the currently-selected member goes unhealthy for 2 consecutive rounds, without ever rewriting singbox-relay.json or restarting the relay (so it never drops existing user connections). The panel (web/server.js + web/app.js) is a pure control-plane consumer: it shells out to residential-helper.sh for every state-changing action (add/remove/enable/disable/global-toggle, always via `enable --add -`/`--remove` reading the URL from stdin so credentials never touch argv), reads singbox-relay.json + .resi-health-state.json + the Clash API directly for read-only status/health display, and — separately from resi-health.sh — runs its own on-demand egress classification probe (ippure.com/ipquery.io/ipinfo.io) for the panel's richer IP/ISP/fraud-score health view. Architecturally this is sound and mostly non-redundant where it looks duplicated (3 different probing purposes, not 3 copies of one probe; 4 domain-keyword-rule emission sites feeding off exactly 1 shared keyword source, not 4 copies of the same data). The genuine cleanup opportunities found are: (1) real, byte-near-identical logic duplication of the curl proxy-config-escaping helper across 3 files/2 languages; (2) a sizeable amount of code (2 full migration functions in update.sh, ~130 lines) that is LEGACY-ONLY for pre-v3.5.7/pre-v3.6.0-R1 installs and can be deleted wholesale under the v4-clean-reinstall decision; (3) one genuinely dead array (LEGACY_DEFAULT_DOMAINS_V3_4_17); (4) a real architectural placement bug where the residential-health-timer's very existence depends on a migration-block code path never invoked on fresh installs; (5) two CLI entry points (interactive menu vs flag subcommand) offering different, overlapping capability levels for the same underlying multi-URL state, with the fuller one undocumented; and (6) the entire non-global/domain-keyword-split code surface (spanning all 4 layers) is a candidate for wholesale removal if the product's committed capability really is only 'residential egress in global mode' as the owner's own capability list states — that determination is the highest-leverage simplification available here but is a product-scope call, not a code-quality bug.
topology_notes:
Hop chain (verified via core.sh + residential-helper.sh, precise file:line in components):
client → [hysteria-residential :40000+41000-50000 (Hysteria2, config-residential.yaml, `outbounds: relay` + `acl: relay(all)`) OR xray vless-residential :10002 (REALITY, xray-config.json, routing rule inboundTag vless-residential → outboundTag relay)] → socks5 127.0.0.1:2080 (b-ui-relay, sing-box, config singbox-relay.json) → resi-pool (type: selector, sticky, switched only via Clash API by resi-health.sh) → resi-N outbound (type: socks version 5, or type: http, depending on residential-proxy.json urls[].type) → residential upstream provider (e.g. Bright Data SOCKS5 22228 / HTTP 44445) → residential exit IP.

DNS handling in the relay: when global=true, ALL DNS queries also go through dns_resi (resolved via the resi-pool detour) per residential-helper.sh:410-417; when global=false, only domain_keyword-matched DNS queries do. Destination domains for TCP/UDP data traffic are passed to the upstream UNRESOLVED (sing-box hands the hostname to the SOCKS5/HTTP CONNECT, not a resolved IP) — confirmed by residential-helper.sh comment at line ~405-407 stating the relay's hot path 'never queries DNS' for pure-HTTP pools.

Two more listeners exist for control/health, both loopback-only: the relay's Clash API on 127.0.0.1:9091 (read by resi-health.sh for switching, and by web/server.js's getRelaySelected() for panel display), and no listener at all for residential-proxy.json itself (plain file, chmod 600, read/written only by residential-helper.sh and web/server.js, both server-local).

No IPv6 anywhere in this subsystem: relay DNS strategy is ipv4_only, UDP:443 (QUIC) is explicitly rejected at the relay to force TCP fallback (residential SOCKS5 generally can't do UDP ASSOCIATE), UDP:53 goes direct, and all other UDP goes direct too — i.e. the residential path is TCP-only in practice.

Egress: everything through the relay ultimately either exits via the chosen residential upstream (SOCKS5 or HTTP CONNECT to the provider) or, in fail-open conditions (empty pool, disabled, or non-matching domain in split mode), via sing-box's own `direct` outbound from the VPS's own IPv4 (never IPv6 — no egress stack on the VPS per CLAUDE.md).

Dependency/egress surface for reproducibility: residential-helper.sh downloads its own sing-box binary from GitHub releases (SagerNet/sing-box, capped at minor 1.14 to avoid 1.15's breaking deprecations) if missing; verify()/resi-health.sh/probeEgress() all make outbound HTTPS calls to third-party IP-info services (api.ipify.org, ipinfo.io, my.ippure.com, api.ipquery.io) as part of normal operation, all from the VPS's own network path (not through the residential upstream) except probeEgress()'s deliberate through-proxy calls.

summary: Wire-level design (BBR, conntrack sizing, port-hop firewall/UDP tuning, hy2 auth moved off HTTP-callback-per-connection, residential SOCKS hop over loopback) is sound and already reasoned about multi-user scale by the author — these are EFFECTIVE and evidenced by comments citing real production incidents. The one genuinely severe defect is NOT on the packet-forwarding path at all: it's in the admin panel's stats-polling code. web/server.js queries per-VLESS-user Xray traffic/online stats by spawning a blocking `execSync` child process (the `xray` CLI) TWICE per user (uplink, downlink), sequentially, with no batching, no caching, and no parallelism. This function is invoked independently by THREE different triggers that overlap in time: a 10s background sync timer, and (whenever an admin has the dashboard open) a 5s browser poll that hits /api/stats and /api/online in the same Promise.all — and each of those two endpoints calls the same per-user Xray query function separately, so a single 5s dashboard tick does the identical O(N) work twice. Node is single-threaded and execSync blocks the event loop, so at N≈1000 vless users this would serialize hundreds to low-thousands of subprocess spawns per tick, starving every other request (subscription endpoints hit by all 1000 clients' apps, JWT auth, user CRUD) for seconds at a time — this is the actual ceiling on "servable to 1000 users," not QUIC/MTU/BBR tuning, which is already handled well. Secondary findings: the b-ui-relay (sing-box) systemd unit — the single mandatory hop for 100% of residential traffic in the "global" mode both production servers actually run — is the only proxy-path service with no LimitNOFILE/MemoryMax/Nice, unlike hysteria-server/hysteria-residential/xray which all get LimitNOFILE=1048576 explicitly. A dead config field (trafficPortResidential:9998) means hysteria-residential's own traffic stats are never polled, so residential-HY2 usage silently never accrues to user quotas. User CRUD still restarts hysteria-server/-residential/xray for every credential-affecting change (mitigated by a no-op content-diff guard added in v3.6.0, but not scoped to just the changed user), so routine admin churn at 1000-user scale still means periodic mass session drops for everyone.

components.name: fetchXrayUserStats() blocking per-user execSync
components.role: Queries Xray gRPC stats (uplink+downlink) for every vless-reality/vless-ws-tls user by spawning `xray api stats` twice per user in a sequential for-loop with execSync (synchronous, blocks Node's single event loop)
components.evidence: web/server.js:1077 `for (const u of users)` then two execSync calls per iteration (lines 1084, 1093), each with `timeout: 3000`. Called from getMergedStats() (line 1136) and fetchXrayOnline() (line 1118) — two independent call sites doing the identical O(N) work. getMergedStats is polled by setInterval every 10000ms (line 1423/1460) and by the on-demand /api/stats handler (line 2068); getMergedOnline (which calls fetchXrayOnline) is polled by /api/online (line 2069). web/app.js:109 `setInterval(load, 5000)` and app.js:114 `Promise.all([api("/users"), api("/online"), api("/stats")])` means every 5s browser tick fires both endpoints, each independently re-running fetchXrayUserStats() — 4x the per-user execSync work per tick, with zero caching between them (verified: no cache/memoize/debounce reference near fetchXrayUserStats in web/server.js).
components.simplification: Replace per-user CLI subprocess spawns with Xray's gRPC StatsService using a persistent grpc client and a single pattern-based query (or the `-pattern` regex form of `xray api stats`) to fetch all users' stats in one round trip; at minimum, memoize/share one fetchXrayUserStats() result per polling tick between getMergedStats and getMergedOnline, and never call it synchronously from a request handler — run it once per interval into a cache and serve reads from that.

components.name: Duplicate Xray stats query within one dashboard tick
components.role: Two unauthenticated-internal API handlers (/api/stats, /api/online) each independently call fetchXrayUserStats(), triggered together by the same browser poll
components.evidence: getMergedStats() line 1136 calls fetchXrayUserStats() directly; getMergedOnline() line 1142 calls fetchXrayOnline() which itself calls fetchXrayUserStats() at line 1118. app.js line 114 fires both endpoints together via Promise.all every 5000ms (line 109). No shared cache exists between the two call paths.
components.simplification: Compute Xray stats once per tick (e.g. in the existing 10s traffic-sync loop) and have both the /api/stats and /api/online handlers read from that cached snapshot instead of re-invoking the subprocess loop.

topology_notes: Traffic path nodes: [client] --QUIC/UDP--> hysteria-server(:PORT+hop range, mode 4 IPv4-only direct egress) | [client] --QUIC/UDP--> hysteria-residential(:40000,41000-50000) --SOCKS5 TCP loopback--> b-ui-relay(sing-box, 127.0.0.1:2080) --TCP/HTTP--> resi-pool upstream. Parallel path: [client] --TCP REALITY--> xray vless-direct(:10001) --freedom/ForceIPv4--> internet, and xray vless-residential(:10002) --socks 127.0.0.1:2080--> same b-ui-relay --> resi-pool. Control/observability plane (NOT on data path but polls it): b-ui-admin (Node, single-threaded, 127.0.0.1:8080 behind Caddy) polls hysteria-server's trafficStats HTTP API on 127.0.0.1:9999 (bulk, one call) and shells out to the `xray` CLI once per vless user per stat direction (not bulk) via 127.0.0.1:<xrayApiPort> gRPC-over-CLI. b-ui-relay's Clash API on 127.0.0.1:9091 is polled by resi-health.sh (systemd timer, ~2min) for selector hot-switch, read-only, does not touch relay's data path. hy2-watchdog.sh (systemd timer, 5min) does a local `ss -lun` port-liveness check only, no network cost. DNS: client-side TUN and server-side subscription both split-route CN-domain-suffix queries to a local/direct resolver and everything else through an https/udp resolver detoured via the proxy outbound itself — no loop back through the tunnel for bootstrapping.
